ruling: DE-RATE on the reported metric; EARLY-STAGE DERAILMENT on the underlying unit metric. Adjusted-EBITDA guidance kept RISING through the drawdown (FY25 $528.8M from $382.4M; Q2-26 guided $160-180M vs $137.5M actual Q2-25; margin guided to 3.0-3.3% of bookings from 2.6%) while the multiple compressed - the HUBS/CTSH/SAP de-rate signature. But rides growth went +16.2% -> +14.5% -> +14.7% -> +11.4% -> +8.5% across five quarters, rides per Active Rider is -7.3% y/y, S&M is +50% y/y to buy that growth, and GAAP operating income is still negative and was WORSE in FY25 (-$188.4M) than FY24 (-$118.9M). The rising metric is adjusted; the falling metrics determine whether it can keep rising. Q2-26 rides, printing 2026-08-06, is the discriminating observation. AMENDMENT (direct estimate-revision test, per the parallel lane's _GATE_TEST_GUIDE_DECEL.md proposal - consensus FY+1 EPS down >3% over trailing 90d, yfinance eps_trend): LYFT FIRES, hard. Current-quarter EPS -8.6%, next-quarter -9.4%, FY26 -13.0%, FY27 -3.2%. Estimates are NOT stable - they are falling fast while the company's ADJUSTED number rises, which is the B-1/B-2 finding restated by a third party: the adjusted line is rising precisely because it excludes what is deteriorating. This upgrades the derailment side of the ruling and moved 4pp from base/bull into bear.
cause: Peak $25.54 on 2025-11-12 after a strong Q3-25 print. Single decisive event: 2026-02-10 AMC Q4-25 print -> -17.0% on 02-11 (74.3M sh, ~7x normal). Three breaks in one release headlined 'Record Q4 and Full-Year 2025 Results': (1) Gross Bookings +19% but revenue only +3%, a ~1,600bp divergence caused by a $168M contra-revenue charge for 'legal, tax, and regulatory reserve changes and settlements'; (2) net income of $2,755.1M economically empty - a $2,897.3M deferred-tax valuation-allowance release, with derived GAAP Q4-25 operating income of -$185.0M and confirmed ZERO goodwill/long-lived impairment; (3) rides growth decelerated to +11.4%. The $1B buyback authorization in the same release did not offset it. Trough $12.46 on 2026-03-30 (drift, no event). Q1-26 print 2026-05-07 produced no move >8%.
honesty_grade: REVIEW - composition divergence, not datum concealment
honesty_note: Marketed takeaway: 'Active Riders growth of 17%', 'Gross Bookings growth of 19%', 'free cash flow of $1.1 billion, an all-time high'. Composition underneath: only ~8.5pp of the 19% bookings growth is volume, ~9.5pp is price/mix (US fares + European taxi mix from FreeNow/Gett); rides per Active Rider is -7.3% y/y; S&M is +50% y/y (5.5% of bookings, +110bps) to acquire those riders; and 62% of the headline FCF is insurance float (35%) plus SBC add-back (27%). Lyft headlines Active Riders - the metric acquisitions and low-frequency cohorts inflate - and never the frequency ratio. Every component is disclosed in the filings and derivable from the company's own metric table, and the $168M charge was footnoted in the bullet that disclosed it. Divergence is in composition and emphasis, not concealment: REVIEW, not ELEVATE.

plan: NO ENTRY at $16.38. Three independent sufficient reasons: (1) PATH - +31.5% off a 126-day-old low and 0.8% under the 3-month high, worst entry geometry in the cycle; (2) PRINT - +/-11.3% implied in three days, last print realized -17.0%, contract forbids blind entry inside two weeks of a print; (3) EDGE - +4.0% against 68.8% IV, nothing paid for; (4) ESTIMATES FALLING INTO A RISING PRICE - FY26 consensus EPS -13.0% over the same 90 days in which the stock rallied ~21%; price and estimates moved in opposite directions over an identical window, which converts the path call from 'late' to 'late AND unsupported'. ENTRY BAND ONLY IF THE PRINT RESETS THE PRICE: $12.50-$14.00 (the fresh-low zone where the risk premium is actually paid), limit-only, starter 0.4-0.5% of the $3.3M deployable ($13-17k). Sits at the BOTTOM of the ruled range by design - the contract sends red-team survivors to the upper half and this is a 4/10, not a survivor. Second tranche only after a print clearing all five bars, never averaged in on price alone.

mode_b_findings: The 19% Gross Bookings headline decomposes to ~8.5pp volume + ~9.5pp price/mix. Rides growth more than halved in five quarters (+16.2% -> +8.5%) while bookings growth held at ~19% on US fare increases and the European taxi mix from FreeNow (closed 2025-07-31) and Gett UK (closed ~May-2026). Read Q2-26 RIDES, not Q2-26 bookings - Gett UK inflates riders and bookings without proportionate rides.

Rides per Active Rider is -7.3% y/y (8.37 vs 9.02). Lyft headlines Active Riders +17% - the metric acquisitions and low-frequency cohorts inflate - and never the ratio, which says the incremental rider is worth less.
They are paying for the growth: Q1-26 S&M $272.9M vs $182.0M = +50.0% y/y on revenue +13.8%; S&M as a share of Gross Bookings 4.4% -> 5.5%, +110bps. That is why operating income is still -$5.3M.
Backing out FreeNow (~4-6M rides/qtr, inferred from Q2-25 +14.5% vs Q3-25 +14.7% growth continuity across the close), ORGANIC rides growth in Q1-26 is ~+6%, down from ~+15% a year earlier.

'All-time-high FCF of $1.1 billion' is 62% non-earnings: insurance-reserve build +$421.5M (35% of TTM OCF; AccruedInsuranceCurrent $1,823.5M -> $2,245.0M) plus SBC add-back ~$316M (27%). Cash earnings ex-float ex-SBC are ~$380-400M, putting the true EV multiple at ~13.7x, not 5x. Float is a liability that gets paid, not profit.

Float is thinly collateralised: insurance reserves (current) $2,245.0M vs restricted cash+investments $1,998.3M = a -$246.7M gap at 3/31/26. Thin, NOT deteriorating (reserves +$64.6M in Q1-26 vs restricted assets +$62.2M).

NEW/UN-NARRATED: the federal mass-tort docket against Lyft is accelerating right now. CourtListener 'v. Lyft, Inc.' captions: 3 (2025 H1), 2 (2025 H2), 12 (2026 Q1, 6 in N.D. Cal.), 11 (2026 Q2, 5 in N.D. Cal.), 14 in the 34 days 2026-07-01 to 08-03 with 13 in N.D. Cal. July captions are anonymised - 'JANE SL110 v. Lyft, Inc.' (3:26-cv-07604), 'S. v. Lyft' x2, 'H.', 'B.', 'C.', 'M.' - initials-only Doe pleadings in Lyft's home district with a SEQUENTIAL plaintiff-numbering convention, the signature of coordinated aggregate litigation. Against a $211.6M loss-contingency accrual (12/31/25) and a $168M charge already taken that cost 17%. Roughly an eight-fold rise in filing rate in five weeks, three days before a print. This is the most likely source of the next negative surprise and it is what makes the thin reserve collateralisation matter: the pool funding the buyback is the pool the docket is aimed at.

AV SYMMETRY WITH THE HOUSE UBER PACK: Uber's bar-3 is 'no new AV-partner defection'. The mirror question for the #2 is whether anything Lyft calls an AV win is differentiated. It is not - Lyft's Q1-26 highlight 'Confirmed our first Baidu vehicles have been secured in the UK' is NON-EXCLUSIVE: Apollo Go began London testing 2026-07-29 'following Lyft, Uber deals'. Uber holds the same partner in the same city. Lyft's only differentiated AV asset is Flexdrive fleet operations (Nashville, opening this fall) - a real asset, and the one leg a Waymo-goes-direct world does not automatically destroy, since an AV owner still needs depots.

THE #2 ASYMMETRY, QUANTIFIED - the mechanism, not a vibe: Lyft's adj EBITDA is 2.7% of Gross Bookings (Q1-26 $132.8M on $4,946.0M), guided to 3.0-3.3%; Uber's rate is roughly 2.5-3x that. Contribution margin in rideshare is concentrated in dense high-utilisation metros - exactly where an AV network enters first - so a 10% loss of bookings in Lyft's top AV-exposed metros removes FAR MORE than 10% of EBITDA, because those bookings carry above-average contribution and the fixed base does not shrink with them. At a 2.7% take there is no buffer and operating leverage runs in reverse violently. THAT - not share loss per se - is the mechanism by which 'AV kills #2 first' is true. And Lyft is US/Canada plus a new European taxi footprint: Waymo's US metro expansion addresses ~100% of the core, while Uber has 70+ countries to spread the same shock.

IS THE AV RISK PRICED? LYFT at ~7.9x EV/FY26E adj EBITDA vs Uber at ~13-14x is a ~43% discount - approximately Lyft's HISTORICAL discount. The market is therefore NOT pricing an AV-specific #2 penalty beyond the ordinary quality discount, and the -35% drawdown was caused by a legal charge and a rides deceleration, not by AV. On this evidence the AV-existential risk is UNPRICED. Most important sentence in the file for anyone tempted by the bounce.

UNDERWEIGHTED BULL LEG: the buyback is real, large and accelerating - 400.9M -> 379.7M shares in five months. FY25's $500.0M against $322.3M of SBC was ~64% dilution-offset, but Q1-26's $300.0M against $86.9M of SBC was overwhelmingly NET retirement. At even half that pace the share count shrinks ~10%/yr at 7.9x EBITDA; if rides merely stabilise, per-share compounding does the work with no re-rating. This is why the score is 4 and not 2.

Management's ADJUSTED EBITDA guidance kept rising (verified) while the sell side cut FY26 GAAP EPS 13% over 90 days. That divergence is the composition-masking finding restated by a third party. It also collides with the path: the stock rallied ~21% over the identical window in which those estimates fell.

edge_explainer: Fairly-paid risk with no edge overlay. Two mechanisms banked. (1) COMPOSITION MASKING IN A TWO-METRIC MARKETPLACE: when a platform reports both a volume metric and a value metric, growth can be sustained in the value metric by price/mix and acquisitions long after the volume metric decelerates - and management will headline the value metric plus a per-user ratio whose denominator the acquisitions inflate. Masking channel = Gross Bookings + Active Riders. Signal channel = rides and rides-per-active-rider, both disclosed and neither headlined. Latency ~1-2 quarters. Structurally IDENTICAL to the UPWK take-rate/GSV divergence courted in the same lane - two different marketplaces, same masking architecture; that recurrence is the transferable finding. (2) FLOAT-FINANCED CAPITAL RETURN: an insurance-float-carrying operator can report FCF that is 35% reserve build, and returning it via buyback is a bet that the reserve is adequate. The tell is not the FCF number - it is restricted assets vs reserves (here -$247M) crossed with the LITIGATION FILING VELOCITY aimed at the reserve. Crossing the docket tape with the reserve gap is the composite nobody prints, and it is a repeatable screen for any float-carrying operator.
unverifiable: TOP GAP: the mass-tort docket counts are page-1 API results, not an exhaustive census, and RECAP coverage of newly-filed dockets is incomplete. Nature-of-suit codes could not be retrieved for the individual N.D. Cal. cases (docket endpoint returned empty for 3:26-cv-07604). The characterisation as coordinated mass-tort filings rests on the caption convention (JANE SL110, initials-only, single district, sequential numbering) - strong circumstantial inference, NOT a read complaint. Load-bearing for the bear.

Uber's EBITDA-to-bookings rate is stated from general knowledge, not recomputed from Uber's filings in this court - re-derive the 2.5-3x relative statement before using it in a sized decision.
Straddle-implied move rests on closing marks with put open interest of 8 on the quoted line, not a live two-sided quote.

Whether the $168M Q4-25 charge is fully behind the company is unknown - described as 'legal, tax, and regulatory reserve changes and settlements' without itemisation, so the split between one-time settlement and ongoing reserve is not determinable from public filings.
Insurance reserves NONCURRENT, if any, were not separately isolated - the float calculation uses AccruedInsuranceCurrent only, so the float share of OCF may be UNDERSTATED.
